operations.normative_notes: The one authenticated step that binds an account-less staged pairing record to an exact AccountId (device-lifecycle.md 2.1.1). The caller is the candidate device itself: it holds the exact device_pairing_request_id and pairing_code, holds the staged candidate key, and authenticates with Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus matching DPoP for a bound pending account handoff. That handoff is the sole source of the exact AccountId, which the candidate signs into device_pairing_target_proof; a server-side side channel or an unsigned request member MUST NOT assert account membership. The Account Authority recomputes the 2.1.2 challenge transcript from its own durable stage, verifies the target signature with the staged new_device_public_key, requires target_proof.account_id to equal the AccountId this handoff is bound to, and only then moves the record from staged to ready_for_claim. The transition is one-way: ready_for_claim never returns to staged and authorized is never reachable without it. Unknown id, pairing_code mismatch, an expired record and a record that is no longer staged all return an indistinguishable not_found. Exact retry of the same canonical intent returns the same outcome without re-attaching a proof; the same request id with different content conflicts. Once the request id locates a retained record, a code mismatch, AccountId/handoff mismatch, transcript/signature/proof mismatch or unusable state counts against the Account Authority's service-private ten-failure ledger keyed only by device_pairing_request_id; an unknown id and an exact successful retry do not. The tenth failure atomically expires staged or ready_for_claim, consumes the code and creates the bounded tombstone, while preserving the existing public error shape and creating no Event, authorization, current state or success outcome. A successful finalize also supersedes: in the same durable transaction it MUST move every other unaccepted ready_for_claim pending record of that AccountId to terminal expired, keeping the bounded tombstone that preserves exact retry and blocks replay, so the account never holds two approvable records at once. This is what makes the existing MUST NOT in device-lifecycle.md 2.1.1 enforceable, and it is the only way v1 retires the code of an earlier pairing attempt; v1 registers no cancel operation. The supersession key is the AccountId alone, so a refreshed pairing page reusing the same candidate key and a different new device with a fresh candidate key retire the earlier record identically, and adding two new devices in parallel is therefore forbidden. Supersession never authors an Event, grants nothing, and never rewrites the terminal outcome of a record pair_device already accepted; an exact retry performs no second supersession. The durable boundary is the gate-side pending ledger, because only the gate side holds the account binding when the Account Authority is deployed separately from the Station. No Arkret Event is authored and nothing is authorized here.
